engagement.request: Establish a practical, industry-aligned (TOGAF) Enterprise Architecture baseline, define the future-state architecture and governance model, and provide a prioritized roadmap supporting growth through 2030.

business_drivers.driver: Hybrid estate has grown through growth, cloud adoption and new digital investments - needs a common architecture baseline
Architecture decisions and standards must be applied consistently across domains
End-to-end visibility of dependencies across applications, data, infrastructure and security
Scalable foundation for future applications, acquisitions (e.g. NACL Industries, 53% stake 2025) and AI adoption
Shift from digital pilots to connected, intelligent, autonomous operations (AI-accelerated R&D, connected product+service, digital agronomy, drones)
Retail network scale-up (1,075 Gromor stores Nov-2025; plan to roughly double) and 1M+ farmer app users

digital_focus_areas.name: AI-accelerated R&D
digital_focus_areas.detail: Formulation, trials, crop response and knowledge reuse

digital_focus_areas.name: Digital agronomy platform
digital_focus_areas.detail: Advisory, satellite insights, orders and service journeys

digital_focus_areas.name: Drone & robotics ecosystem
digital_focus_areas.detail: Hardware, prescription maps, telemetry and operations

digital_focus_areas.name: Data, AI & EA foundation
digital_focus_areas.detail: Data domains, APIs, cloud, security, MLOps and governance

in_scope: Business, Application, Data, Technology architecture (TOGAF B-D)
Cross-cutting: Security, Integration, AI, Governance, Transition
out_of_scope: SAP RISE (ERP) detailed assessment - dependencies captured only
OT systems detailed assessment - dependencies captured only
constraints: Microsoft-centric stack (Azure, SQL Server, Entra ID SSO, M365/Copilot)
DC Hyderabad + DR Chennai + Azure hybrid

principles_cil.name: Cloud-smart on Azure
principles_cil.statement: New workloads default to Azure PaaS/containers; DC Hyderabad hosts only what must stay on-prem.

principles_cil.name: Clean-core ERP
principles_cil.statement: Keep SAP S/4HANA (RISE) standard; extend side-by-side via APIs, not core modifications.

principles_cil.name: API-first integration
principles_cil.statement: Systems integrate through governed APIs/events, not point-to-point file drops or DB links.

principles_cil.name: One farmer, one record
principles_cil.statement: Farmer, dealer and product data have a single owner and system of record shared across retail, app and agronomy.
principles_cil.togaf_basis: Principles 10-14 (Data is an Asset / Shared / Trustee / Common Vocabulary)

principles_cil.name: Acquisition-ready architecture
principles_cil.statement: A standard integration playbook (identity, finance, master data) onboards acquired entities like NACL within 2 quarters.
principles_cil.togaf_basis: Principle 2 Maximize Benefit to the Enterprise

principles_cil.name: Human-in-the-loop for agronomy
principles_cil.statement: AI recommendations that affect farmer inputs or spend are reviewed or confirmable by an agronomist or the farmer.

principles_cil.name: Grounded and explainable AI
principles_cil.statement: Generative AI answers cite their source data/documents; no ungrounded advice in farmer channels.

principles_cil.name: Privacy by design (DPDP Act 2023)
principles_cil.statement: Farmer and employee personal data is classified, consented and minimised before any AI use.

principles_cil.name: Shared AI platform, no shadow AI
principles_cil.statement: AI use cases run on the common Azure AI/ML platform with MLOps, not isolated vendor tools.

principles_cil.name: AI value tracked
principles_cil.statement: Every AI initiative has a measurable business KPI and an owner, reviewed by the ARB.

guardrails.name: No new point-to-point links to SAP or retail
guardrails.statement: New integrations to SAP and retail go through the governed API layer.

guardrails.name: SAP core stays standard
guardrails.statement: No core modifications in SAP S/4HANA; extensions are side-by-side.

guardrails.name: SSO for every user-facing app
guardrails.statement: All user-facing applications, including subsidiaries, authenticate through Entra ID.

guardrails.name: Tier-1 apps have tested DR
guardrails.statement: Tier-1 applications have defined RPO/RTO and a DR test in the last 12 months.

guardrails.name: Farmer PII never leaves governed AI services
guardrails.statement: Personal data is masked or excluded before use in any external AI model.

guardrails.name: Human approval for agentic actions with spend
guardrails.statement: AI agents may not commit spend, credit or farmer-facing advice above set limits without human approval.

guardrails.name: Every data domain has a named owner
guardrails.statement: No new system of record goes live without a business data owner and quality rules.

guardrails.name: Buy before build
guardrails.statement: Custom builds need ARB approval showing no fit-for-purpose SaaS or SAP option exists.

patterns.name: API-led integration
patterns.use: System, process and experience APIs through one gateway

patterns.name: Side-by-side ERP extension
patterns.use: Extend SAP outside the core through released APIs and events

patterns.name: Event-driven data sharing
patterns.use: Publish master and transaction events once for many consumers

patterns.name: Cloud-native on containers
patterns.use: New custom apps on the container platform with CI/CD

patterns.name: Grounded GenAI (RAG)
patterns.use: Assistants answer from governed, cited enterprise content

patterns.name: Human-in-the-loop agents
patterns.use: Agents propose; people approve above risk thresholds

engagement_plan.note: Indicative timeline, subject to stakeholder availability, data access and consolidated feedback. Hybrid team approach.

phases.objective: Stand up the team and governance, agree the assessment framework and align CIL stakeholders on scope.
approach: Mobilise the KPMG and CIL teams; set governance, cadences and delivery controls
Define the assessment framework, viewpoints, information requirements and the function-wise focus group plan
Align stakeholders on scope, architecture domains, exclusions and review gates
phases.gate: Scope, framework and review gates agreed with the CIO

activities.name: Mobilize project team & establish the engagement governance, stakeholder structure, communication cadences, and delivery controls.
Define the assessment framework, architecture viewpoints, information requirements, function wise focus group discussion plan, and repository structure.
Align CIL stakeholders on the scope, architecture domains, exclusions, working approach, and review gates.

phases.name: As-Is Assessment & Gap Analysis
phases.objective: Baseline the business, application, data, technology and governance landscape and agree the prioritised gaps.
approach: Run function-wise workshops on business needs, application challenges and future expectations
Assess data, analytics and AI; infrastructure, cloud and backup; network, identity, security and resilience
Evaluate EA governance maturity, then prioritise and validate gaps with business stakeholders
phases.gate: As-Is Assessment & Gap Analysis Report accepted at the W8 steering committee

activities.name: Conduct workshops to understand business needs, application challenges, and future expectations.
Assess the current data, analytics, and AI landscape and planned capabilities.
Review the current infrastructure, cloud, backup, and deployment architecture.

approach: Set industry-aligned principles, technology standards, reference patterns and design guardrails

Develop transition states for priority areas and validate them with CIL stakeholders
phases.gate: To-Be Enterprise Architecture validated with CIL stakeholders (W13)

activities.name: Define Industry-aligned architecture principles, technology standards, reference patterns, and design guardrails.
Develop the target application and integration architecture covering portfolio, deployment, APIs, events, and data exchange.
Define the target data and AI architecture covering platforms, governance, analytics, AI services, security, and MLOps.

Define the target network and security architecture covering connectivity, identity, access controls, resilience, and observability.
Develop transition-state architectures for priority areas.
Validate the target architecture, standards, patterns, and transition designs with CIL stakeholders.
To-Be Enterprise Architecture

activities.name: Translate prioritized gaps into quick-win and strategic modernization initiatives.
Prioritize and sequence initiatives based on business needs, risk, complexity, effort, and dependencies.
Develop a two-to-five-year roadmap covering initiative sequencing, dependencies, and transition stages.
Define the EA operating model, including roles, governance forums, review mechanisms, and KPIs.

Initiatives, Prioritized Roadmap & TOM

scope_of_work.requirement: Establish a practical, industry-aligned (TOGAF, etc.) Enterprise Architecture baseline for CIL, define the future-state architecture and governance model, and provide a prioritized roadmap supporting growth through 2030.
scope_of_work.objective: Assess the current IT architecture, identify technology gaps, define standards and target-state designs, establish a sustainable EA operating model and create an actionable short to long term transformation roadmap.

items.title: Current-state discovery & architecture baseline
items.activities: Map business capabilities to the application landscape and document current application, integration, data, infrastructure, network, cloud, security and AI architecture views.

items.title: Domain assessment & prioritized gap analysis
items.activities: Assess architecture fitness, lifecycle, resilience, scalability, interoperability, security and operational dependencies; prioritize gaps by business and technology impact.

items.title: Target-state architecture & standards
items.activities: Define industry-aligned principles, standards, reference patterns and domain target architectures, including transition views for priority areas.

items.title: AI architecture & adoption direction
items.activities: Assess current & potential AI initiatives and define enterprise direction across use cases, data, platforms, models, security, governance and operating capabilities.

items.title: EA operating model, governance & repository
items.activities: Define roles, architecture forums, change-control checkpoints, review templates, compliance scoring, KPIs and a maintainable, editable architecture repository.

items.title: Transformation roadmap
items.activities: Sequence quick wins and strategic initiatives over two to five years, capture dependencies and directional effort, and establish repeatable architecture guidance for future needs.

viewpoints.name: Enterprise overview
viewpoints.concerns: Where CIL stands today, what changes and why, cost and risk to 2030
viewpoints.purpose: The single picture of the CIL estate for people who fund and steer the programme. It shows today's landscape, the target state for 2030 and the transition between them in one place, without technical detail, so the board and sponsors can see what is changing, why, and at what cost and risk.
questions: Where does CIL's architecture stand today across business, applications, data and technology?
What changes by 2030, and which business drivers does each change serve?
What does the roadmap cost, in which years, and is it affordable within planned IT spend?
Which risks need a decision from the steering committee now?
viewpoints.used_in: Steering committee (W4, W8, W12, W16) and board updates; opens every playback.
viewpoints.where: Dashboard: domain health, ADM status, current-to-target state comparison, architecture landscape

viewpoints.name: Business capability
viewpoints.concerns: Capability maturity, criticality, business–IT alignment, process gaps
viewpoints.model_kind: Capability map, heat map, EPC process model
viewpoints.purpose: How well each business capability is performed today, measured from the owners' questionnaire answers, and where weak maturity meets high business criticality.
questions: Which capabilities are critical but immature?
Where do business and IT disagree on how well systems support the work?
Which L3 processes are the root cause of each gap?
viewpoints.used_in: Function-head playbacks and the As-Is Assessment report (W8).
viewpoints.where: Business Architecture: discovery, heat map, criticality × maturity, gap register, EPC process models

viewpoints.name: Application portfolio
viewpoints.concerns: Portfolio fit, lifecycle, duplication, technical debt, dispositions
viewpoints.model_kind: Portfolio catalog, layered view, communication diagram
viewpoints.purpose: The application portfolio judged on business and technical fit, technical health and duplication, with a rule-based disposition and written rationale for every application.
questions: Which applications to invest in, retain, modernise, replace or consolidate?
Where is technical debt or a single point of failure concentrated?
Which capabilities have duplicate or no application support?
viewpoints.used_in: Application owner reviews and the rationalization workshop.
viewpoints.where: Applications: intake, capability view, rationalization, technical health, gap register

viewpoints.name: Integration
viewpoints.concerns: Interfaces, patterns, point-to-point debt, API governance
viewpoints.purpose: How applications exchange data, which integration patterns are used and where point-to-point or manual re-keying creates risk.
questions: Which interfaces are point-to-point or manual?
Which applications are integration hotspots?
What API and event standards should apply?
viewpoints.used_in: Integration design reviews and the ARB.
viewpoints.where: Applications: interaction view, interface catalogue, integration & API view

viewpoints.name: Data & AI
viewpoints.concerns: Ownership, quality, privacy (DPDP), lineage, AI readiness
viewpoints.purpose: Ownership, quality, privacy and lineage of each data domain, and whether the data is ready for the AI initiatives that depend on it.
questions: Who owns each data domain and where is it mastered?
Which domains hold personal data under DPDP 2023, and are they protected?
Which AI initiatives are blocked by data quality or ownership?
viewpoints.used_in: Data governance council and AI use-case prioritisation.
viewpoints.where: Data & Technology: data domains, data assessment, data architecture, data flow & AI readiness

viewpoints.name: Infrastructure, network & cloud
viewpoints.concerns: Hosting, DR, network, landing zones, platform lifecycle
viewpoints.purpose: Where applications run, how plants, depots and offices connect, and whether hosting, DR and landing zones are fit for scale and resilience.
questions: Which platforms are end-of-life or non-standard?
Is DR adequate for critical applications?
Is the cloud landing zone ready for new workloads?
viewpoints.where: Data & Technology: platforms, sites & network, infrastructure view with network, cloud and hosting details

viewpoints.name: Security & resilience
viewpoints.concerns: Identity, zero trust, monitoring, recovery, compliance
viewpoints.purpose: Identity, security monitoring and recovery controls across the estate, and where compliance obligations are not yet met.
questions: Are identity and access controls consistent across applications?
Can CIL detect and recover from an incident within tolerance?
Which resilience checks fail or are unknown?
viewpoints.used_in: CISO risk reviews and audit committee updates.
viewpoints.where: Data & Technology: resilience & standards checklist, security layer of the infrastructure view

viewpoints.name: Investment & roadmap
viewpoints.concerns: Priorities, sequencing, effort, affordability, benefits and risks
viewpoints.model_kind: Initiative list, prioritisation matrix, wave roadmap, budget
viewpoints.purpose: The prioritised set of initiatives that close the gaps, sequenced into waves with indicative cost, benefits, risks and affordability against the IT budget.
questions: Which initiatives come first, and why?
What does each wave cost and what does it deliver?
Does the roadmap fit within planned IT capex?
viewpoints.used_in: Steering committee investment decisions and the final roadmap (W16).
viewpoints.where: Roadmap & Governance: long list, prioritisation, roadmap and budget; IT Budget

tailoring.rationale: Light-touch: principles, guardrails and governance set up in weeks 1-3 rather than a separate phase.
Vision statements, drivers and stakeholder viewpoints produced as specified.
Baseline assessed to L3 through questionnaires; target expressed as rated layered views and gap hypotheses.
Gaps consolidated into initiatives, prioritised and sequenced in waves with indicative cost.
ARB charter, checkpoints and compliance levels defined; project-level compliance reviews start after the engagement.
Out of the 16-week scope; the repository update process covers ongoing change.
Core entities only: capability, process, application, interface, data domain, platform, location, gap, initiative.
Viewpoint catalogue maps each stakeholder concern to the view that answers it.
Traceability held in the data (capability → app → data domain → hosting), not as formal correspondence rules.
Decision log on Roadmap & Governance records each decision with the principles it applies.
